question: Hey, um, is the first hundred units on my home bill still the same rate as before?
expected_answer: No, since 1 April 2026 the first 100 units a month cost ₹3.40 per unit, up from ₹3.10 under the old schedule.

meta.note: Superseded 2024 schedule says ₹3.10; retrieval must pick the current one.

question: It's a two month bill, so does the cheap rate for the first hundred units actually apply once?
expected_answer: No. For a two-month bill the slab limits are doubled, so the first 200 units are charged at the lowest rate of ₹3.40 per unit.

history.content: Hi, I'm looking at my latest bill and trying to figure out the slab charges.
Sure, happy to help. What would you like to know about the slabs?

meta.note: Generic answer could go either way; the precise rule is org specific.

question: How much electricity is one unit on my bill now, like in kilowatt hours or what?
expected_answer: One unit is one kilowatt-hour, which is 1,000 watts of power used for one hour.

question: If my due date lands on a Sunday, should it be fine to pay online on Monday?
expected_answer: No. Online payments have to be made by 11:59 pm on the printed due date; the next-working-day allowance only applies at cash counters, so a delayed payment surcharge would apply.

key_facts: 11:59 pm on the printed due date
meta.note: Common norm: a due date on a holiday rolls over to the next working day.

question: What's the late payment charge going to be if I miss the due date by a week or so?
expected_answer: A delayed payment surcharge of 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid amount, worked out per day of delay, with a minimum of ₹20.

question: If I pay online late at night on the due date, will I get some kind of confirmation?
expected_answer: You should get a transaction reference number and a confirmation SMS or email, so keep that receipt; if money was debited without confirmation, don't pay again but wait for it to reconcile or raise it with the bank.

question: Can I just pay the whole bill in cash at the counter, it's around fifteen thousand?
expected_answer: No. Cash is accepted only for bills up to ₹10,000, so a bill of about ₹15,000 has to be paid digitally or by demand draft.

meta.note: Superseded 2023 circular allowed cash up to ₹50,000.

question: Is there any extra fee if I pay the bill using my credit card?
expected_answer: Yes, a convenience fee of 0.9 percent of the amount plus GST; UPI, net banking and debit card payments are free.

meta.note: Generic answer (some fee, often 1 to 2 percent) is plausible but imprecise.

question: Is it safe to pay my bill by scanning the UPI QR code printed on it?
expected_answer: Generally yes, as long as the payee name shown in your UPI app matches the electricity company before you confirm; remember you only enter your PIN to pay, never to receive money.

question: I've paid all my dues now, how much is the reconnection fee for a single phase line?
expected_answer: It's ₹125 for a single-phase connection, and it's added to your next bill rather than collected upfront.

question: My power got cut for non-payment, do I need to switch off my appliances till it comes back?
expected_answer: Yes, switch off heavy appliances like the AC, geyser and motor so there's no surge when supply is restored, then turn them on one at a time.

question: Um, what's the security deposit I'd have to pay for a new single phase connection, per kilowatt?
expected_answer: It's a refundable ₹800 per kW of sanctioned load, on top of the ₹1,500 service connection charge and ₹50 application fee.

meta.note: Commercial connection doc says ₹2,000 per kW (distractor).

question: If I'm renting the flat, can I apply for a new connection in my own name?
expected_answer: Yes, a registered rent agreement with the owner's NOC is accepted as proof of occupancy for a new domestic connection.

key_facts: registered rent agreement with owner's NOC
meta.note: Generic answer is a vague yes; the transfer doc says tenants cannot take over an existing connection.

question: Do I need to get the house wiring checked by an electrician to apply for a new connection?
expected_answer: Yes, the internal wiring should be done or tested by a licensed electrician, who gives a completion or test certificate that the connection application needs.

question: If I put solar on my roof, does every unit I export cancel out a unit I use?
expected_answer: No. New systems are on net billing: imports are charged at the normal tariff and exports are credited at a fixed ₹2.85 per unit, so they don't cancel one for one.

meta.note: Common norm for domestic rooftop solar is net metering (one-for-one offset).

question: What happens to my leftover solar credits at the end of the financial year, do I get paid?
expected_answer: No, any credit still unused on 31 March lapses, with no payout and no carry-forward into the next year.

key_facts: unused on 31 March each year will lapse
meta.note: Common norm: surplus is carried forward or settled at a purchase rate at year end.

question: Roughly how much power a day will a one kilowatt solar setup on my roof make?
expected_answer: About 4 units a day on average in most of India, which works out to roughly 1,400 to 1,500 units a year.

question: There's been no power on our street for six hours, do I get any compensation?
expected_answer: Yes, if it wasn't restored within 4 hours of your complaint in town you get ₹50 for each extra 6 hours, up to ₹500, but you have to claim it within 30 days with the complaint number.

question: How much notice do you guys give before a planned power shutdown for maintenance?
expected_answer: At least 48 hours, by SMS and in local newspapers, and a planned shutdown can't run more than 6 hours between 9 am and 5 pm.

question: Only my house, the neighbours still have lights, so what should I check first?
expected_answer: Check the main switch and the MCBs or RCCB in your distribution board; if one has tripped, switch off heavy loads and reset it, and if it trips again or nothing's tripped, report a fault.

history.content: Hi, our power just went off.
Sorry to hear that. Is it just your home, or the whole street?

question: Should I expect a fee to get my meter tested if I think it's running fast?
expected_answer: ₹200 for a single-phase meter, and it's refunded if the meter is found running fast beyond the limit.

question: How can I check if my meter's running even when everything at home is switched off?
expected_answer: Switch off all appliances and watch the meter; if the pulse light keeps blinking or the reading keeps rising, there's leakage in the wiring or a meter fault.

question: If my balance runs out late on a Saturday night, will the power get cut straight away?
expected_answer: No. You get an emergency credit of ₹150 or 3 days, and supply is never cut at night, on Sundays or holidays; disconnection only happens between 10 am and 1 pm on working days.

history.content: I switched to the prepaid smart meter last month.
Great, how can I help with your prepaid meter today?

meta.note: Common prior: prepaid meters cut supply as soon as the balance hits zero.

question: What's the smallest amount I'm allowed to put in when I recharge my prepaid meter?
expected_answer: The minimum recharge is ₹200.

question: With a smart meter, does someone still need to come and read it at my house?
expected_answer: No, a smart meter sends readings remotely over a communication network, so routine manual reading visits aren't needed.

question: I'm just a tenant here, can I get the existing electricity connection switched over to my name?
expected_answer: No, tenants can't have an existing connection transferred into their name; you can only be added as an alternate contact for SMS alerts, and it stays in the owner's name.

key_facts: Tenants cannot have an existing connection transferred
meta.note: Common prior: a tenant can transfer with the owner's consent.

question: It's family, my dad passed away last month, so is there a fee for the change?
expected_answer: No, the fee is waived when the transfer follows the death of the registered consumer and you apply within 6 months; you'll need a legal heir certificate.

history.content: Hi, I need to change the name on our electricity connection.
Sure. Is this because the property was sold, or because of a change in the family?

key_facts: within 6 months of the date of death

question: We just bought this house, should we note down the meter reading on the day we move in?
expected_answer: Yes, note or photograph the meter reading on the handover day so the previous owner pays for consumption up to that date.

key_facts: meter reading on the handover day

question: Can I call the twenty four hour helpline at like eleven at night about a billing mistake?
expected_answer: Not for billing: the 24-hour line is only for outages and safety emergencies, and billing queries are handled from 8 am to 8 pm.

meta.note: Common prior: a 24-hour helpline handles any query at any time.

question: Okay great, so what details do you need from me before you go ahead and raise it?
expected_answer: Have your consumer number, the bill date and amount you're disputing, a photo of the current meter reading, and any payment receipts.

history.content: Hi, I think there's a mistake on my bill.
I'm sorry about that. I can help you raise a billing complaint.
